name: Steam
mfaNote: Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator (time-based codes) and Steam Guard email codes. Steam does not support passkeys or FIDO2 hardware keys — the mobile authenticator is the strongest option.
scamPatterns: Fake item or trade offers that redirect to a login page; "Free gift card" or "free game" direct messages; Fake Steam Support messages asking for your password or Steam Guard code; Third-party trade sites that ask for your API key

name: Discord
mfaNote: Discord supports two-factor authentication via an authenticator app, plus passkeys (passwordless login) and hardware security keys (FIDO2).
scamPatterns: Links that steal your Discord token or session; Fake Nitro giveaways and "free boosts"; "Verify your account" QR codes that hand over your session; Fake Discord staff or support direct messages

name: Epic Games
mfaNote: Epic supports two-factor authentication via authenticator app, email, or SMS.
scamPatterns: Free V-Bucks or cosmetic scams; Fake Epic login pages; Account-trade and account-selling scams

name: EA
mfaNote: EA supports login verification via authenticator app or email.
scamPatterns: FUT coins or in-game currency scams; Fake EA Help phishing pages; Account-selling and account-takeover scams

name: Riot Games
mfaNote: Riot supports two-factor authentication via email and authenticator app.
scamPatterns: Skin and account giveaway scams; Fake tournament invitations; "Free Riot Points" or free currency scams

name: PlayStation
mfaNote: PlayStation supports 2-step verification via authenticator app or text message, plus passkey sign-in.
scamPatterns: "Free PSN codes" scams; Fake Sony or PlayStation support calls; Account-deactivation phishing links

name: Xbox
mfaNote: Xbox accounts use Microsoft two-step verification (authenticator app or passwordless).
scamPatterns: "Free Game Pass" or free subscription scams; Fake Microsoft support calls; Gift-card refund and account-takeover scams
